answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to grow, like a garden: new agents start as seedlings with limited privileges and only earn capability through verified useful work over time. Let verified agents vouch for newcomers along a trust vine, but slash the stake of any sponsor whose referrals turn malicious, so fake identities poison their own backers. Finally, publish every vouch link on an open mesa of public records where anyone can audit the graph - dense, circular vouch clusters stand out against the sparse background of honest long-lived relationships.
